product.title: Sports Analytics Team Builder
product.summary: Three struggling franchises, one mission — rebuild each within its budget using the numbers.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students rebuild an MLB roster within budget against stated statistical thresholds, then unlock an NBA scenario, then an NFL one, each with its own metrics and cap. One progress bar tracks all three, and finishing all three opens a shared victory screen.
product.technology: multi-page static site with shared JS state, seeded from a spreadsheet via a Python extraction script

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Complete and publicly reachable, with an earlier prototype retained in-repo showing a finished refactor. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. Scenario 1 can be passed without reading a single statistic.
knownBlockers: No real optimisation: every player in the Scenario 1 pool clears the team-average pass thresholds alone, so any pair satisfying the position rules passes. Spending the minimum $34M produced the same result as spending the full $40M.
A page error fires on every scenario completion: "Cannot set properties of null (setting textContent)".

curation.tierBasis: A good premise defeated by its data: every player in the pool clears the thresholds alone, so any legal pair passes and minimum spend equals maximum spend.

provenance.evidence: 201-M3-L2/league-select.html gates NBA behind MLB completion ('🔒 Complete MLB First') and NFL behind NBA; all three share js/game-state.js and redirect to one victory.html. Recorded as one experience, not three.
